title: How do you prepare for a CMS survey of staff training?
description: How CMS surveyors review hospital and nursing home staff training using State Operations Manual Appendices A and PP, with the tags and a document checklist.
shortAnswer: To prepare for a Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) survey of staff training, keep personnel files that show required training and demonstrated competency, including contract and agency staff, and make sure staff can explain what they were trained to do. Surveyors following the State Operations Manual review personnel files, interview staff, and observe care. Hospital surveys are unannounced, and nursing home training is cited under Appendix PP tags beginning at F940.
keyTakeaways: State Operations Manual Appendix A (hospitals) says certification is accomplished through observations, interviews, and document and record reviews, and that all hospital surveys are unannounced.
Hospital surveyors review personnel files to determine whether staff have the required education and training and are licensed where required.
For restraint and seclusion, hospitals must document training and demonstration of competency in personnel records, initially at orientation and periodically, for contract and agency staff too.

Appendix PP guidance for nursing homes expects staff to demonstrate competency in training topics, the facility to keep a record of trainings, and training before staff work independently with residents.
Nurse aides need at least 12 hours of in-service training a year, and Appendix PP states the survey team does not need to find a negative outcome to cite tag F947.

sections.heading: How do CMS surveyors assess staff training?

blocks.text: CMS surveyors, usually from the State Survey Agency, assess training through record review, interviews, and observation, using the interpretive guidelines and survey procedures in the State Operations Manual (SOM) appendices. [Appendix A](https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/guidance/manuals/downloads/som107ap_a_hospitals.pdf) (Rev. 248, issued September 18, 2026) states that certification of hospital compliance "is accomplished through observations, interviews, and document/record reviews," and that "All hospital surveys are unannounced."

Appendix A's information gathering task lists personnel files among the records to review, "to determine if staff members have the appropriate educational requirements, have had the necessary training required, and are licensed, if it is required." Nursing homes are surveyed under the Long-Term Care Survey Process, with guidance to surveyors in [Appendix PP](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/provider-enrollment-and-certification/guidanceforlawsandregulations/downloads/appendix-pp-state-operations-manual.pdf).

Training findings often start from a care problem. Appendix PP tells surveyors, where deficient care practices are identified, to review the training nurse aides received in the corresponding subject area, and its probes for resident rights training combine staff interviews, observation of staff interactions, and review of training documentation.

sections.heading: What do surveyors check for hospital staff training?

blocks.text: In hospitals, surveyors check that the training each Condition of Participation requires exists, was delivered to the right staff including contractors, and is documented with evidence of competency. Restraint and seclusion is the most explicit example in Appendix A.

blocks.title: Appendix A, tag A-0208 (42 CFR 482.13(f)(4))
blocks.text: "Staff personnel records must contain documentation that the training and demonstration of competency were successfully completed initially during orientation and on a periodic basis consistent with hospital policy." Surveyors review a sample of staff personnel records, "including contract or agency staff."

items: **Restraint and seclusion program.** Survey procedures ask whether the hospital has a documented training program and documented evidence that all levels of staff with direct care responsibilities, including agency or contract staff and others such as security guards who may apply restraints, are trained and can demonstrate competency.
**Trainer qualifications (A-0207).** Surveyors review personnel files of people who provide the training and ask whether the hospital has a system for documenting that trainers are qualified.

**Emergency preparedness.** 42 CFR 482.15(d) requires initial training for new and existing staff, contractors, and volunteers, training at least every two years, documentation, and demonstrated knowledge of emergency procedures.
**Infection prevention and antibiotic stewardship.** 42 CFR 482.42 requires competency based training and education of personnel, including medical staff and contracted personnel as applicable.

**Newer requirements.** Annual training under 482.43(c) (transfer policies) and 482.55(c) (emergency services readiness) took effect July 1, 2025, and obstetrical services training under 482.59(c) takes effect January 1, 2027.

blocks.text: Each of these is explained on the [CMS hospital Conditions of Participation training page](/regulations/cms-hospital-conditions-of-participation-training). Accredited hospitals may also be assessed against [Joint Commission staff competency requirements](/regulations/joint-commission-staff-competency-requirements).

sections.heading: Which tags apply to nursing home training?

blocks.text: Nursing home training requirements in 42 CFR 483.95 are cited under a series of tags beginning at F940 in Appendix PP. F940 covers the overall training program and, per the guidance, is cited when a facility fails to implement training for multiple topics; the topic tags cover specific requirements.

blocks.text: The F940 guidance states that staff should "be able to demonstrate competency in the topic areas of the training program," that the facility "is also expected to keep a record of these trainings," and that training requirements should be met "prior to staff and volunteers independently providing services to residents, annually, and as necessary based on the facility assessment." Requirements are summarized on the [CMS nursing home training page](/regulations/cms-nursing-home-training-requirements).

For F947, Appendix PP says adequacy may be measured not only by documented in-service hours but by demonstrated competencies, through written exams or consistent application of interventions, and that webinars should not be used alone.
Because hospital surveys are unannounced, the checklist below describes a standing state of readiness, not an event. It is an original checklist drawn from Appendices A and PP.

items: Personnel files for employees, contract, and agency staff that show orientation training, required periodic training, licensure, and demonstrated competency where the rule requires it.

A training matrix linking each regulatory training requirement to roles, frequency, and the competency check used. The [training matrix for a hospital](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix-for-a-hospital) shows one approach.
Trainer qualification records for restraint and seclusion and other specialist training.
For nursing homes, the facility assessment and evidence that the training program reflects it (483.71 and F940).
Nurse aide in-service hour totals per aide for the year, with topics and links to performance review findings.
Emergency preparedness training records and exercise documentation.
Curricula with learning objectives, performance standards, and evaluation criteria, which Appendix PP describes as supporting current standards of practice.
A process for tracking participation, so any person's file can be produced during the survey.

sections.heading: How should staff be prepared for surveyor interviews?

blocks.text: Surveyors interview staff to test whether training translated into knowledge, so preparation means effective training and regular checks rather than rehearsed answers. Appendix A procedures repeatedly direct surveyors to interview staff to determine whether they can demonstrate required abilities and whether practice matches policy.

items: Run periodic competency checks on high risk topics such as restraint use, infection prevention, and emergency procedures, and keep the results.
Include night, weekend, agency, and contract staff in competency checks, since surveyors may interview anyone on shift.

Use incidents and grievances to target refresher training, as Appendix PP links nurse aide training to identified weaknesses. See [how to measure training effectiveness](/guides/how-to-measure-training-effectiveness).

sections.heading: Which version of the guidance applies?

blocks.text: Appendix A was last revised as Rev. 248 on September 18, 2026. The Appendix PP text quoted here is Rev. 225 (issued August 8, 2024); CMS's long-term care survey revision history records that an official revised Appendix PP was added in May 2025 following memo QSO-25-14-NH, so confirm the current tag text before relying on any detail. CMS is also implementing a risk-based survey approach that gives consistently higher performing nursing homes a more focused survey, which is expanded immediately if resident safety concerns arise.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each Condition of Participation or requirement for participation to role based learning outcomes and competency checks, so a facility can show not only completion but demonstrated competency for employees, agency staff, and contractors. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences) and [audit evidence](/platform/audit-evidence).

faqs.q: Do contract and agency staff need training records for a CMS survey?
faqs.a: Yes, where the requirement covers them. Appendix A tells surveyors to review restraint and seclusion training records including contract or agency staff, and 42 CFR 483.95 requires nursing home training for individuals providing services under contract and for volunteers, consistent with their roles.

faqs.q: Is completion of an online module enough for CMS?
faqs.a: Often not. Restraint and seclusion rules require documented demonstration of competency, and Appendix PP guidance expects nursing home staff to demonstrate competency in training topics, with webinars not to be used alone for nurse aide in-service training.

faqs.q: Can a nursing home be cited for training without resident harm?
faqs.a: Yes. Appendix PP states that the survey team does not need to find a negative outcome to cite a deficiency at F947, the nurse aide in-service tag. Missing hours or required topics can be cited on the records alone.

faqs.q: Does a hospital get notice before a CMS survey?
faqs.a: No. Appendix A states that all hospital surveys are unannounced and instructs surveyors not to give hospitals advance notice. Training records, competency evidence, and staff knowledge therefore need to be survey ready at all times, including on night and weekend shifts.

Appendix PP Rev. 225 (08-08-24): F940 intent text (demonstrate competency, keep record, training prior to independently providing services, annually, as necessary per facility assessment; staff includes contracted staff and volunteers; F940 cited for failure across multiple topics); F941-F947 tag headings map to 483.95(a)-(g); F942 probes (interview, observe, review training documentation); F947 guidance (12 hours minimum, webinars not alone, demonstrated competencies, no negative outcome needed to cite, review training where deficient care practices identified).
